title: Mock 2 · Planning and Products
blurb: Goal setting, TVM, debt-repayment strategies (with a short caselet) and the everyday product facts an adviser quotes to clients.

questions.q: Pooja saves about ₹20,000 a month. She sets a goal that needs her to invest ₹50,000 a month starting next month. Which goal-setting feature is missing?
questions.explanation: Goals must be specific, measurable, realistic and time-bound. A goal requiring ₹50,000 a month when only ₹20,000 can be saved is not realistic; the workbook uses exactly this kind of example.
hints: The amount is specified, so it is specific.
₹50,000 a month is measurable.
It starts next month, so time is defined.
Correct: it exceeds her saving capacity.

questions.q: An investment of ₹50,000 grew to ₹80,000 in 4 years. What is its CAGR (approximately)?
hints: Correct.
This is the simple average (60% / 4) and ignores compounding.
This is the absolute (total) return.
This value does not satisfy 50,000 x (1+r)^4 = 80,000.

questions.q: What is the monthly EMI on a home loan of ₹25 lakh for 20 years at 8.5% per annum (monthly rests, payments at month end)?
hints: This is the EMI at 8%, not 8.5%.
This is interest of the first month plus nothing for principal; not an EMI.
Correct.
Too high; does not match PMT for these inputs.

questions.q: According to the workbook, an emergency fund should ideally cover:
options: Six months of expenses, held in liquid assets
Twelve months of income in equity funds
questions.explanation: The emergency fund should be the first savings goal and cover about six months of expenses in liquid assets; if income is secure it can be laddered with about three months in liquid assets.
hints: Too small and based on income instead of expenses.
Correct.
Equity is unsuitable for emergency money.
Not the workbook norm.

questions.q: A lender charges 2.5% per month on a short-term loan. What is the approximate effective annual cost?
questions.explanation: Effective annual cost = (1 + 0.025)^12 - 1 = 34.49%. Simply multiplying 2.5% by 12 (30%) ignores compounding.
hints: This ignores monthly compounding.
This is the effective cost at 2% per month.
Not linked to the data.
Correct.

questions.q: What is Rohan's debt-to-income ratio, and how should it be read?
options: 37.5%; in the 35-40% zone that the workbook calls excessive
questions.explanation: Monthly debt servicing = 30,000 + 9,000 + 6,000 = ₹45,000. DTI = 45,000 / 1,20,000 = 37.5%. A ratio higher than 35% to 40% is seen as excessive.
hints: This uses only the home-loan EMI.
This is the rupee figure (₹45,000) mistaken for a percentage.
Correct.
Not related to the given numbers.
questions.case: Rohan earns ₹1,20,000 a month. He pays EMIs of ₹30,000 (home loan, ₹28 lakh outstanding at 8.25%), ₹9,000 (car loan, ₹3 lakh outstanding at 10%) and ₹6,000 (personal loan, ₹60,000 outstanding at 15%). He also carries a credit card balance of ₹90,000 at 38% a year. He wants to become debt-free faster and asks you how to order repayments.

questions.q: If Rohan follows the snowball method, which debt does he attack first?
questions.explanation: The snowball method starts with the smallest outstanding amount regardless of interest rate, to build momentum. The smallest balance is the ₹60,000 personal loan.
hints: Correct: smallest balance first.
The credit card would be first under the avalanche method (highest rate).
Not the smallest balance.
Largest balance; it would be last.
questions.case: Rohan earns ₹1,20,000 a month. He pays EMIs of ₹30,000 (home loan, ₹28 lakh outstanding at 8.25%), ₹9,000 (car loan, ₹3 lakh outstanding at 10%) and ₹6,000 (personal loan, ₹60,000 outstanding at 15%). He also carries a credit card balance of ₹90,000 at 38% a year. He wants to become debt-free faster and asks you how to order repayments.

questions.q: Under the blizzard method, what is the correct order of repayment for Rohan?
options: Credit card, personal loan, car loan, home loan
Home loan, car loan, credit card, personal loan
Personal loan, car loan, credit card, home loan
Personal loan, credit card, car loan, home loan
questions.explanation: Blizzard begins like snowball (smallest balance: personal loan) and then switches to avalanche (highest remaining rate: credit card at 38%, then car loan at 10%, then home loan at 8.25%).
hints: This is the pure avalanche order.
This is a reverse order with no logic.
After the first loan, blizzard switches to highest rate, so the credit card must come next.
Correct.

He pays EMIs of ₹30,000 (home loan, ₹28 lakh outstanding at 8.25%), ₹9,000 (car loan, ₹3 lakh outstanding at 10%) and ₹6,000 (personal loan, ₹60,000 outstanding at 15%). He also carries a credit card balance of ₹90,000 at 38% a year. He wants to become debt-free faster and asks you how to order repayments.

questions.q: Under the SEBI (Self-Regulatory Organizations) Regulations, 2004, a Self-Regulatory Organisation is an organisation of intermediaries recognised by SEBI that:
questions.explanation: The definition expressly excludes a stock exchange. An SRO must abide by SEBI's directions, SEBI nominates directors on its board and it must report members' violations to SEBI.
hints: The definition specifically excludes stock exchanges.
Correct.
SROs in the securities market are recognised by SEBI.
SROs must always abide by SEBI's directions.

questions.q: A company offers 8,000 shares in a book-built issue with a price band of ₹200-₹240. Bids received: ₹240: 1,500; ₹235: 2,000; ₹230: 3,000; ₹225: 2,500; ₹220: 1,000 shares. What is the cut-off price?
questions.explanation: Cumulative demand from the top: 1,500 (₹240), 3,500 (₹235), 6,500 (₹230), 9,000 (₹225). The 8,000 shares are fully subscribed at ₹225, which becomes the cut-off.
hints: At ₹230 cumulative demand is only 6,500, short of 8,000.
At ₹220 demand is 10,000, but the issue is already covered at a higher price.
Correct.
At ₹235 demand is only 3,500.

questions.q: The difference between the yield on a corporate bond and the yield on a government security of the same maturity is called:
questions.explanation: Credit spread is the extra yield (risk premium) corporates pay for default risk; higher default probability means a wider spread.
hints: Correct.
Coupon yield is coupon / face value.
Current yield is coupon / market price.
Basis is futures price minus spot price.

questions.q: A stock has a P/E of 18 and expected EPS growth of 24% a year. Based on its PEG ratio, the stock appears:
questions.explanation: PEG = P/E / growth = 18 / 24 = 0.75. A PEG below 1 suggests the price has not fully reflected the growth, i.e. undervalued.
hints: PEG is not 1 here.
This inverts the formula (24/18).
The number is right but a PEG below 1 means undervalued.
Correct.

questions.q: A bond with face value ₹100 pays a coupon of 7.5% and trades at ₹96. What is its current yield?
questions.explanation: Current yield = annual coupon / market price = 7.50 / 96 = 7.81%.
hints: This is the coupon yield (coupon / face value).
Correct.
This multiplies by 0.96 instead of dividing.
This is the discount to face value.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes a futures contract from a forward contract?
options: Futures are standardised and traded on an exchange with a clearing house guaranteeing settlement
Futures terms are negotiated privately between two parties
Futures carry higher counterparty risk than forwards
Futures cannot be used for hedging
questions.explanation: Futures are standardised forwards traded on an exchange; the clearing corporation becomes counterparty and both sides pay margins. Forwards are bilateral OTC contracts.
hints: Correct.
That describes forwards.
Forwards carry higher counterparty risk; futures reduce it.
Futures are widely used for hedging.

questions.q: To be classified as a large cap fund, a scheme must invest at least ___ of total assets in companies ranked ___ by full market capitalisation.
questions.explanation: Large cap companies are those ranked 1 to 100 on AMFI's list; a large cap fund must invest at least 80% of total assets in them.
hints: 65% is the mid cap and small cap requirement.
Ranks 101-250 are mid caps, not large caps.
Correct.
This is the mid cap fund definition.

questions.q: The main benefit of investing a fixed sum every month through an SIP is:
options: Buying the same number of units every month
Rupee cost averaging: more units when NAV is low, fewer when it is high
questions.explanation: Because the same amount buys more units when prices are low and fewer when high, the average cost per unit falls over time: rupee cost averaging.
hints: SIPs carry market risk; no return is guaranteed.
Exit loads still apply as per scheme terms.
The amount is fixed, so the number of units varies.
Correct.

questions.q: A PMS portfolio grew from ₹50 lakh to ₹60 lakh in year 1 (profit-share charged) and fell to ₹55 lakh in year 2. Under the high-water mark principle, a profit-sharing fee will next be charged only when the value:
options: Returns to the hurdle rate on ₹55 lakh
questions.explanation: The high-water mark is the previous peak on which fees were paid (₹60 lakh). No profit-sharing fee is charged until that level is crossed.
hints: ₹55 lakh is the current, lower value.
Correct.
₹50 lakh is the original investment, already surpassed.
The hurdle applies only after the high-water mark is exceeded.

questions.q: Which pair correctly states two SEBI conditions for every AIF scheme?
options: Corpus of at least ₹20 crore and no more than 1,000 investors
Corpus of at least ₹100 crore and no more than 200 investors
Corpus of at least ₹5 crore and unlimited investors
Corpus of at least ₹20 crore and public advertisement allowed
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a corpus of at least ₹20 crore and cannot have more than 1,000 investors; funds can be raised only by private placement.
hints: Correct.
Both numbers are wrong.
Corpus is wrong and investors are capped at 1,000.
AIFs cannot solicit the public; only private placement is allowed.

questions.q: If two securities have a correlation coefficient of +1, combining them in a portfolio:
options: Reduces risk below that of either security
Provides no diversification benefit; portfolio risk is the weighted average of their risks
questions.explanation: With perfect positive correlation, the portfolio standard deviation equals the weighted average of the individual standard deviations; the risk-return line is straight and there is no diversification benefit.
hints: Risk can be eliminated only with perfect negative correlation and the right weights.
That needs correlation below +1.
Correct.
Risk is a weighted average, not doubled.

questions.q: A portfolio holds three stocks: 50% in a stock with beta 1.4, 30% with beta 0.9 and 20% with beta 0.6. What is the portfolio beta?
questions.explanation: Portfolio beta is the weighted average: 0.5 x 1.4 + 0.3 x 0.9 + 0.2 x 0.6 = 0.70 + 0.27 + 0.12 = 1.09.
hints: This is the simple average of the three betas.
Not the weighted average.
That is only the highest beta.
Correct.

questions.q: The document that records an investor's objectives, constraints, risk tolerance and review process, and guides all portfolio decisions, is the:
questions.explanation: The Investment Policy Statement (IPS) is the road map for the portfolio: it sets realistic expectations, guides the manager, provides an evaluation framework and protects the investor against inappropriate decisions.
hints: The KIM is an abridged mutual fund offer document.
Correct.
The PMS disclosure document describes the manager's fees and risks, not the client's objectives.
The SID describes a mutual fund scheme.

questions.q: Which investor can use the PAN exemption for micro investments in mutual funds?
options: An individual investing ₹40,000 in total in a fund house over 12 months
An individual investing ₹75,000 in one SIP year
questions.explanation: Micro investments up to ₹50,000 in aggregate per fund house (rolling 12 months or financial year) by individuals are exempt from PAN; HUFs and non-individuals are not eligible.
hints: Correct.
HUFs are not eligible for the exemption.
Non-individuals are not eligible.
₹75,000 exceeds the ₹50,000 limit.

questions.q: The number of clients of a part-time investment adviser shall not exceed ____ at any point of time.
questions.explanation: A part-time investment adviser can have at most 75 clients in total at any point of time and must use the term 'part-time investment adviser' in correspondence.
hints: Not the regulatory cap.
300 clients is the trigger for an individual IA to move to non-individual registration.
Correct.
Not the regulatory cap.

questions.q: An adviser repeatedly switches a client from one product to another mainly to earn fresh commissions. This practice is called:
questions.explanation: Frequent switching to increase commission earnings is churning, listed in the workbook among wrong practices; it is one reason SEBI separated advice from distribution.
hints: Rebalancing restores a target allocation for the client's benefit.
TAA is a portfolio decision, not a commission practice.
Front running is trading ahead of client orders; not what is described.
Correct.

questions.q: A customer complained to her bank but received no satisfactory resolution. After how long can she approach the RBI Integrated Ombudsman?
questions.explanation: If a complaint to the bank is not satisfactorily resolved within one month, the customer can approach the Integrated (Banking) Ombudsman.
hints: Too short.
Correct.
Three months is the Insurance Ombudsman's award timeline.
Too long.
